description: Open-ended jazz-theory explanations, graded 1-5 by an LLM judge on correctness + coverage of the listed key points. RAG should help with grounding/depth.

items.q: Why does a tritone substitution (e.g. Db7 in place of G7 resolving to C) work? Explain the shared notes.
points: G7 and Db7 share the tritone (B and F), which are the 3rd and 7th guide tones
those guide tones resolve the same way into C (B→C, F→E)
creates smooth/chromatic bass motion Db→C
both are dominant function toward C

items.q: Explain the 'backdoor ii-V' (e.g. Fm7–Bb7 resolving to Cmaj7).
points: Fm7–Bb7 is the ii-V of Eb (relative/parallel), borrowed from C minor
Bb7 is the bVII7 of C
it resolves deceptively/by common tones to Cmaj7 instead of Eb
common substitute for the standard ii-V (Dm7-G7)

items.q: Why is the altered scale a good choice over a V7alt chord (e.g. G7alt going to C)?
points: it contains the altered tensions b9, #9, #11(b5), b13(#5)
it is the 7th mode of the melodic minor (Ab melodic minor over G7)
those tensions create maximum tension that resolves strongly to the I
it omits the natural 5th and 9th

items.q: Explain modal interchange (borrowed chords) and give a clear example of borrowing iv in a major key.
points: borrowing chords from the parallel mode/key (e.g. parallel minor)
iv in C major = Fm (or Fm7) borrowed from C minor
creates a darker/plagal color, often iv→I
common examples: bVII, bVI, iv, iiø7

items.q: What is the function of a secondary dominant (e.g. V7/V) and how does it create forward motion?
points: a dominant chord that targets a chord other than the I (tonicizes it)
V7/V in C = D7 targeting G7
introduces a chromatic leading tone (F# for D7) outside the key
creates momentum/pull toward the target chord

items.q: Why do Coltrane changes (Giant Steps) move by major thirds, and why are they hard to improvise over?
points: the tonal centers cycle by major thirds (e.g. B–G–Eb), dividing the octave equally
each key center has its own ii-V or V-I, moving very fast
rapid key changes leave little time to outline each new tonality
requires memorized patterns / strong key-center awareness

items.q: Explain the difference between a ii-V-i in a minor key vs a ii-V-I in a major key (chord qualities and scales).
points: minor: iiø7 (half-diminished), V7(b9/alt), i-(minor)
major: ii-7, V7, Imaj7
minor V often uses harmonic minor / altered; major V uses mixolydian
the ii in minor is m7b5 vs m7 in major

items.q: Explain tension and resolution in a dominant 7th chord using the tritone between its 3rd and 7th.
points: the 3rd and 7th of a dominant form a tritone (unstable interval)
e.g. in G7 the tritone is B–F
the tritone resolves inward/outward to the tonic chord tones (B→C, F→E for C)
this drives the V→I resolution
